cases.name: New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen

components.decision: Invalidated New York’s special-need condition for a public-carry license.
components.scope: Protects public carry for ordinary self-defense; does not invalidate all objective licensing requirements.
components.locator: Thomas majority opinion Parts II and IV; footnote 9.
components.survey_fit: The poll addresses this named licensing condition. Its simpler self-protection wording does not measure approval of the historical-tradition test.

cases.interpretation_limit: Direction refers to firearm rights, not liberal ideology. The 52.6% point estimate is a narrow lead, not a significance finding.

cases.name: United States v. Rahimi

components.issue: Temporary disarmament after a judicial threat finding
components.decision: Allowed temporary disarmament following a court finding of a credible physical threat.
components.scope: Facial challenge to the restraining-order statute; the Court’s conclusion is narrower than a ban on everyone described as an abuser.
components.locator: Roberts majority opinion Part II and concluding paragraph.
components.survey_fit: The poll names domestic abusers broadly but omits the judicial finding and temporary duration. Its 74.0% estimate is related context, not exact approval of all statutory conditions.

cases.interpretation_limit: Do not turn a broad group label in the poll into a conclusion about every restraining order or lifetime disarmament.
